email.body1:
Bill, saw Team D3 completed its move into Symetri, now Autodesk's largest global partner across 25,000-plus customers.

A combination that size usually opens far more in-market accounts than the field team can cover before they cool, and that is where pipeline quietly slips during integration. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Symetri off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Bill, quick follow-up for Symetri.

Integrating two go-to-market motions usually raises the pipeline target faster than coverage can adjust, and most teams cannot say how many meetings they need to hit the combined number. The gap shows up late, mid-quarter.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Symetri needs to close that gap, and where it breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Bill, last bit of proof for Symetri.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Symetri's reply rate likely compares to other technology-services teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?
email.body4:
Bill, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority during the integration, no problem at all. Merging brands and teams is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a partner-led sales motion? I will tailor it to Symetri either way.
